title: High-Skill AI Wage Premium by 2030
description: Projected change in wages for workers with strong AI/ML skills relative to the median, measuring the emerging 'AI premium' in compensation.

history.proxyContext: UK job vacancies; US premium likely higher based on PwC/Lightcast data
Willingness-to-pay premium reported by 45% of leaders; likely understates actual market premium

sources.title: The Wage Divide is Widening Again and AI May Be to Blame
sources.excerpt: Demand for high-wage jobs with salaries over USD $100,000 has grown by about 150% over the past two years. Meanwhile, job postings for low-wage positions have fallen steadily for nearly two years.

sources.title: AI Job Postings and Salary Trends
The AI Talent Landscape: Skills, Demand, and Compensation
Microsoft FY24 Q3 Press Release
sources.excerpt: Microsoft Cloud revenue was $35.1 billion, up 23%. More than 65% of the Fortune 500 now use Azure OpenAI Service, and $100M+ Azure deals increased over 80% YoY.

sources.title: AI talent comes at a 30% salary premium
sources.excerpt: Companies hiring AI talent face a 30% salary premium as demand far outstrips supply, with experts warning that the cost of delayed AI hiring will only increase over time.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence and Jobs: Evidence from Online Vacancies
sources.publisher: Journal of Labor Economics (Acemoglu, Autor, Hazell, Restrepo)
sources.excerpt: AI-exposed establishments reduce hiring in non-AI positions. A wage premium of 11% exists for job postings requiring AI skills within the same firm.

sources.title: Beyond the Buzz: Developing the AI Skills Employers Actually Need
sources.excerpt: Analysis of 1.3B job postings finds AI skills command 28% salary premium (~$18K/year); 43% for workers with 2+ AI skills. 51% of AI-skill postings now outside IT/CS with 800% growth in non-tech gen AI roles since 2022.

sources.title: OECD Skills Outlook 2025
NVIDIA 2025 Proxy Statement
sources.excerpt: NVIDIA median employee total compensation was $301,233 in FY2025 (ending January 2025), with CEO-to-median pay ratio of 166:1. Total headcount reached 36,000, a 21.6% increase YoY.

sources.title: OpenAI is paying workers $1.5 million in stock-based compensation on average
sources.excerpt: OpenAI average stock-based compensation reached $1.5M per employee in 2025. Research scientist total compensation ranges from $763K to $1.44M. The company raised $6.6B in October 2024 at a $157B valuation.

sources.title: AI reports and resources
sources.excerpt: LinkedIn's AI skills resources hub tracking AI engineering talent growth (130% increase since 2016). 7 out of every 1,000 LinkedIn members globally are AI engineering talent.

sources.title: PwC AI Jobs Barometer 2025: The AI Wage Premium
sources.excerpt: Workers with AI skills now command a 56% wage premium over non-AI peers, up from 25% just one year prior. AI roles median compensation reaches $157K.

sources.title: AI Salary Statistics 2026: Global Compensation Trends
sources.excerpt: AI/ML engineers median total compensation reached $185K in 2025, with top-tier researchers commanding $500K-$1M+. The premium over general software roles widened to 35%.

sources.title: Experimental Evidence on the Productivity Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence
sources.excerpt: ChatGPT compressed productivity distribution — low-ability workers gained most (40% time reduction, 18% quality increase). May reduce skill premium over time.

sources.title: Generative AI at Work
sources.excerpt: AI assistance increases customer service worker productivity by 15% on average. Less experienced workers improve most; AI disseminates best practices from top performers.

sources.title: Bridging Skill Gaps for the Future: New Jobs Creation in the AI Age
sources.excerpt: Job postings with 4+ new skills pay up to 15% more (UK) and 8.5% more (US); middle-skill roles being squeezed while high-skill workers gain.

sources.title: Task-Specific Technical Change and Comparative Advantage
sources.excerpt: some occupations — such as architects, engineers, and executives — see absolute wage declines

sources.title: Labor Market Effects of Generative AI
sources.excerpt: Adoption concentrated among younger, college-educated, higher-earning employees, reinforcing wage premium for AI-complementary skills.

sources.title: How AI is affecting productivity and jobs in Europe
sources.publisher: CEPR VoxEU (Aldasoro, Gambacorta, Pál, Revoltella, Weiss, Wolski)
sources.excerpt: The wage gains observed may accrue disproportionately to highly skilled workers, potentially widening income inequality.

sources.title: AI is simultaneously aiding and replacing workers, wage data suggest
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas (J. Scott Davis)
sources.excerpt: Nominal average weekly wages nationwide have increased 7.5 percent, while the computer systems design sector has risen 16.7 percent — a 9.2 percentage point gap reflecting the AI-skill wage premium.

sources.title: Should you still major in computer science?
sources.excerpt: The median salary for early-career CS majors was $90,000 in 2024. The median salary for all recent college graduates was just $55,000.

sources.title: Labor market impacts of AI: A new measure and early evidence
sources.excerpt: Workers in the most exposed professions earn 47% more, on average, and are 16 percentage points more likely to be female

sources.title: The Geography of AI Jobs — Indeed Hiring Lab
sources.excerpt: AI-related roles offer a 38% wage premium in top-10 tech metros vs. national average. Non-AI roles in same metros show only 12% premium.

sources.title: Conversation starter: are AI jobs booming or overhyped?
sources.excerpt: AI jobs pay more than similar jobs that do not focus on AI, with a typical premium of 25%. The share of AI jobs among new job listings increased 123% from 2023 to 2024.

sources.title: AI is driving mass layoffs in tech, but it's boosting salaries by $18,000 a year everywhere else, study says
sources.excerpt: Job postings for non-tech roles that require AI skills offer 28% higher salaries — an average of nearly $18,000 more per year. The divide between AI-skilled and non-AI-skilled workers is widening.

sources.title: The Skills Mismatch Economy: Insights from the Wharton-Accenture Skills Index
sources.excerpt: AI is redistributing economic value away from routine cognitive tasks toward judgment, coordination, and specialized knowledge.

sources.title: Augmenting or Automating Labor?
sources.excerpt: Augmentation AI fosters new work and raises wages for high-skilled occupations.

sources.title: Job Transformation, Specialization, and the Labor Market Effects of AI
sources.excerpt: AI raises the return to social and non-routine manual skills, while reducing the return to analytical skills. Workers with high analytical skills are thus over-represented among those who lose from the AI shock.

sources.title: The New Map of AI Work: San Jose Builds It & New York Scales It
sources.excerpt: AI professionals earn $215,000, on average, in San Jose, CA — the highest in the country. But, with living costs 13% above average, that premium narrows. For comparison, in Dallas–Fort Worth, TX, $128,000 salaries stretch further with costs just 3% above average.

sources.title: Skills or degree? The rise of skill-based hiring for AI and green jobs
sources.excerpt: AI skills and expertise are highly valued by employers, offering a 23% wage premium, compared to a 13% wage premium for Master's degrees and a 33% premium for PhDs. In science, engineering, and tech jobs, the AI skills premium is 36%. Analysis of over 10 million online job vacancies in the UK between 2018 to 2024.

sources.title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Learning curves
sources.excerpt: early adopters with high-skill tasks have more successful interactions with Claude than later, less technical adopters. These early-adopting users may simultaneously be the most exposed to AI-driven disruption and most aided by AI in these initial, augmentative waves of adoption.

sources.title: AI Narrows Performance Gaps — But Does That Mean It Reduces Inequality?
sources.excerpt: If AI dramatically boosts the productivity of high-paying knowledge work while leaving lower-paid service occupations largely unaffected, between-occupation inequality could widen even as within-task inequality narrows.

sources.title: Expertise
sources.excerpt: automation has raised wages and reduced employment in occupations where it eliminated inexpert tasks, but lowered wages and increased employment in occupations where it eliminated expert tasks.

sources.title: AI Quarterly Pulse Survey Q1 2026
sources.excerpt: 45% of leaders are willing to pay 11% to 15% more for strong AI skills
